title: Plasmodium Species — Key Features
description: Flip each card to review the distinguishing features of each Plasmodium species.

dialogs.answer: Malignant tertian malaria. Fever: irregular 48 hr. Infects ALL ages of RBCs (normal-sized). Banana-shaped gametocytes, multiple ring forms, appliqué (accolé) forms. Causes cerebral malaria, severe anaemia, blackwater fever.

tips.front: Think: 'falciparum = fatal' — the only species causing malignant malaria.

dialogs.answer: Benign tertian malaria. Fever: 48 hr. Infects reticulocytes only → enlarged RBCs. Schüffner's dots, ameboid trophozoites. Hypnozoites in liver → relapse. Radical cure requires primaquine.

tips.front: Think: 'vivax = vivid dots' — Schüffner's dots are the hallmark.

dialogs.answer: Benign tertian malaria (mild). Fever: 48 hr. Infects reticulocytes → slightly enlarged, oval/fimbriated RBCs. Schüffner's dots present. Also has hypnozoites → relapse possible.

tips.front: Think: 'ovale = oval RBCs' — fimbriated edges are the clue.

dialogs.answer: Benign quartan malaria. Fever: 72 hr (unique among species). Infects senescent (old) RBCs → normal or smaller size. Band-form trophozoites. Ziemann's stippling (rare). Associated with nephrotic syndrome.

tips.front: Think: 'malariae = 72 hours' — the only quartan species.
